abstracts: High-resolution remote-sensing images play a vital role in advancing solar photovoltaic (PV) system deployment, which is crucial for renewable energy generation. Urban rooftops are widely recognized as optimal platforms for PV deployment, and the accurate identification of multi-type rooftops using remote-sensing images is essential for effective PV capacity planning. However, existing image segmentation models face challenges in rooftop segmentation, particularly in addressing ambiguous edges and variations in rooftop scales. To address these challenges, we propose RoofX-Net, a novel decoder within an encoder–decoder framework designed to enhance the precision of rooftop segmentation. RoofX-Net introduces two key modules: (1) the Edge Extraction Module, which employs hand-crafted edge-computing kernels for improved edge detection, and (2) the Scale Awareness Module, which addresses scale variations by generating geometric awareness at different scales, with a specific focus on small-scale rooftops. We conduct a comprehensive evaluation of RoofX-Net on the WHU dataset and our established Rooftop+ dataset, which is specifically curated to support multi-type rooftop segmentation. RoofX-Net demonstrated superior performance across both datasets. Notably, on the Rooftop+ dataset, our model achieves an overall accuracy of 96.39%, a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 90.75%, and an F1-score of 95.11%, outperforming the compared models. RoofX-Net is versatile and can be integrated into existing segmentation frameworks, offering enhanced performance with minimal additional cost. In practical urban planning projects, our method significantly reduces planning time while maintaining reliability, demonstrating substantial potential for optimizing solar PV deployment in urban environments. The implementation of the proposed method is publicly available at https://github.com/K-Y-Chen/RoofX-Net.

abstracts: Building damage captioning is an emerging task within damage extraction, playing a crucial role in damage assessment and decision-making tasks. However, the complexity of disaster-affected environments and the diversity of damage manifestations make it challenging for current models to accurately identify damage features and generate comprehensive captions. To advance the development of building damage captioning and improve caption accuracy, this study constructed a dataset namedBD-CCand proposed a building damage feature keyword-guided caption model (KGBDCNet). In terms of dataset, the BD-CC dataset focuses on building damage in the Mariupol region, collecting a total of 4300 pairs of high-resolution RGB dual-temporal remote sensing images obtained from Google Earth. This includes 2877 pairs of images showing damaged buildings and 1423 pairs showing undamaged buildings, with all damage resulting from human conflict. Regarding the model, this paper utilizedLoRAto fine-tune theRemote-CLIPfor efficient extraction multi-modal features of damaged buildings. To fuse multi-modal features, this paper designed thecross-modal attention guided module (CAGM), which employs aretrieve-enhance strategyto guide damage keywords to enhance the visual feature representation of damage information. This paper further proposed thespatial–temporal memory-enhanced module (STMEM), which significantly improves the model’s recognition accuracy for changed regions and its ability to capture temporal evolution by establishing the dynamic associations of spatial–temporal features between bi-temporal images. The benchmarked experiment of the BD-CC dataset was conducted using current state-of-the-art methods to validate its effectiveness. On the public datasetLEVIR-CCand the self-built datasetBD-CC, comparison experiments were conducted betweenKGBDCNetand other methodsto test the model’s advancement. Additionally, we integrated alarge language modeland damaged grade judgement criteria to achievezero-shot building damage assessmentbased on the captions generated by the model, testing itsrobustness and generalizability. In the aforementioned experiments, the proposed method achieved superior results, demonstrating its effectiveness. The code of the proposed method will be made available at https://github.com/Lucky-DW/KGBDCNet.

title: Causally regularized full-resolution channel attention and frequency refinement for cloud removal in satellite imagery

abstracts: Optical remote sensing images are essential for Earth surface analysis; however, their applications are limited by cloud occlusion, as annual global cloud coverage exceeds 60%. The introduction of temporal compensation has addressed the limitation of single-image approaches, which struggled with thick cloud cover. The integration of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data has further improved their cloud removal performance. Nevertheless, existing methods still face notable challenges. Specifically, they lack fine-grained, long-range compensation and adaptive mechanisms to effectively distinguish the high-frequency information from noise. Moreover, current approaches lack an optimization mechanism to ensure the acquisition of the most representative features. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel Optical–SAR fusion method for cloud removal that explicitly combines controlled spatio–temporal aggregation with causal regularization (CR). A pixel-wise channel attention (PCA) module with high-frequency refinement (HRR) is introduced to enable full-resolution feature extraction while introducing frequency compensation advantages under acceptable computational complexity. Temporal attention aggregation is applied to facilitate effective temporal compensation. Furthermore, the CR module is employed to suppress statistically correlated but semantically irrelevant features arising from Optical–SAR fusion and temporal aggregation, improving robustness and generalization. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real-world datasets confirm the effectiveness of the proposed spatio–temporal feature extraction architecture, showing measurable yet modest metric improvements and state-of-the-art generalization under realistic cloud contamination. https://github.com/wjven/CR-PCA-HRR.

abstracts: 3D building instance change detection enables the monitoring of changes in individual building entities, serving as a critical means for security warning and urban management. Existing methods typically adopt a ​​multi-stage approach​​ based on multiple independent task-specific models to sequentially address instance segmentation and change detection in a decoupled manner. However, these methods not only increase computational complexity but also struggle to leverage the synergistic relationships among multiple tasks to enhance change detection performance. Furthermore, existing change detection datasets lack instance-level annotations, which impedes the development of deep learning-based 3D instance change detection methods.​ Thereby, we expand upon existing 3D point cloud change detection datasets by introducing new building instance labels, resulting in a publicly available urban 3D Building instance Change Detection dataset, named 3DBiCD. It integrates photogrammetric and LiDAR point clouds to characterize 3D building instance change across Hong Kong, China, and Utrecht, Netherlands, with 10,501 building instances, of which 2044 instances change, exhibiting a 19.5% change ratio. Moreover, we propose a Multi-task Synergistic Enhancement Network, named MSENet, which achieves end-to-end 3D building instance change detection in a single-stage approach and leverages inter-task synergy to enhance change detection performance. Specifically, it integrates two innovative modules, the Instance Cluster Mask (ICM)module and the Instance-oriented Change Refinement (ICR)module, to unify instance segmentation and change detection within a single framework. The ICM module processes change-rich encoded features through a clustering-guided feature fusion approach to output precise instance masks​, and the ICR module integrates the instance-specific geometric and semantic cues to refine foreground instance change features. Experiments show that MSENet achieves 83.06% and 92.54% of the mean of IoU over building changes on realistic point clouds, leading to an improvement of 3.97% and 2.87% over the state-of-the-art, demonstrating the efficiency of MSENet. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/MSENet and https://github.com/zhanwenxiao/3DBiCD.

title: Towards individual agricultural parcel vectorization from VHR imagery: A coarse-to-fine and multi-task learning method

abstracts: The vectorization of agricultural parcels is a foundational step in precision agriculture, enabling the monitoring of crop status and yield estimation. Existing methods struggle with two primary challenges: (1) overlapping parcels, caused by inaccurate localization in densely arranged fields, and (2) merged parcels, resulting from an inability to distinguish spectrally similar neighbors with narrow boundaries. We introduce IAPVec, a robust vectorization framework that leverages the Segment Anything Model (SAM) to address these limitations. Our approach integrates two key innovations: a coarse-to-fine prompt filter that refines region proposals to minimize overlaps, and a point-line ambiguous boundary enhancement module that explicitly guides the model to learn critical corner points and edge features. To support this research, we contribute the CAPCAD dataset—a large-scale, very high-resolution (0.5 m) benchmark with polygon annotations of 14,889 images, covering over 620 km2 of diverse agricultural parcel construction areas in China. Comparative experiments confirm that IAPVec sets a new state-of-the-art, outperforming existing methods by absolute gains of unless 1.8% in mask-focused metrics and 1.1% in boundary-focused metrics. This demonstrates its potential as a vital tool for advancing precision agricultural management and food security. The code is at https://github.com/ANAN200202/IAPVec.

title: Robust detector-free multimodal image matching based on visual model guidance and gated attention

links.context: cal-Infrared, Optical-SAR, Optical-Map, and Optical-Depth) demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing detector-based and detector-free baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness. abstracts: Multimodal image matching is a crucial foundational task for multi-source information fusion. However, severe geometric distortions and Non-linear Radiometric Differences (NRD) pose significant challenges to robust matching, such as the poor repeatability of keypoints. While detector-free methods emerge to mitigate this, current approaches relying on global context capture inadvertently aggregate irrelevant background noise, leading to reduced feature discriminability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a multimodal image matching method based on Visual Model Guidance and Gated Attention. First, we design a dual-stream backbone network that performs multi-scale fusion of high-level semantic priors from a visual foundation model with local geometric features from standard convolutions. This effectively enhances feature robustness against NRD and guides the model to focus on content-consistent regions. Second, to resolve the feature over-smoothing caused by global interactions, we propose a Gated Linear Attention (GLA) module. By employing a dynamic gating mechanism to filter out irrelevant global background noise, this module maximizes the preservation of local feature discriminability while incorporating effective long-range dependencies. Finally, we construct a coarse-to-fine multi-stage matching pipeline that cascades robust coarse matching with precise pixel-level refinement, achieving high-precision correspondence. Extensive experiments on four multimodal datasets (Optical-Infrared, Optical-SAR, Optical-Map, and Optical-Depth) demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly outperforming existing detector-based and detector-free baselines in terms of accuracy and robustness. The implementation of the proposed method will be made publicly available at https://github.com/yeyuanxin110/VMGGA.

title: Fine-grained heterogeneous change detection in complex disaster response with wavelet-based spatial-frequency coupled learning

abstracts: Heterogeneous remote sensing change detection (CD) based on optical and SAR imagery is essential for rapid disaster monitoring, as it overcomes single-sensor limitations and enables all-weather observation. However, the inherent heterogeneity between optical and SAR modalities—stemming from their disparate imaging mechanisms—results in poor feature comparability, significantly impeding fine-grained, accurate change identification. To address the issue, this study explores a combination of data-level strategies and methodological enhancements. First, to alleviate the data scarcity, this study constructs two sub-meter (0.35 m) heterogeneous datasets tailored for earthquake building damage and flood assessment, thereby providing a high-resolution data foundation for fine-grained disaster monitoring. Second, a Siamese Spatial–Frequency Coupled Network (SSFCNet) is introduced to mitigate the cross-modal discrepancy. Specifically, a Spatial-Frequency Coupled Encoder (SFCE) is designed to simultaneously model spatial semantics and frequency directional features via wavelet transforms, thereby aligning heterogeneous representations while mitigating noise. To refine change representation, an Explicit Change Guidance Module (ECGM) is designed to incorporate distinct difference priors into the decoding stage. Subsequently, a Multi-scale Inverse Wavelet Decoder (MIWD) exploits the invertibility of wavelet transforms to restore high-frequency details, preventing information loss during upsampling. Finally, a Boundary-Aware Loss (BAL) is devised to enforce geometric consistency along change boundaries through gradient constraints. Extensive experiments on five public datasets and the two newly constructed datasets demonstrate that SSFCNet significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy and boundary integrity. Notably, the proposed method achieves an optimal balance between performance and computational efficiency, demonstrating its potential for rapid, robust emergency response. For reproducibility, our code and data are available at https://github.com/yangyang12318/SSFCNet.

title: MiMNet-STASF: a spatiotemporal decoupled network for sub-pixel canopy structure retrieval of urban forests with multi-source long-term remote sensing time series

Together with cross-regional GEDI-referenced evaluation, these results support MiMNet-STASF as an effective and scalable solution for management-oriented, fine-grained urban forest canopy-structure mapping. abstracts: Forest canopy height (FCH) and vertical structural composition are essential for urban ecological assessment and precision forest management, yet reliable retrieval in fragmented urban–rural transition landscapes remains challenging due to multi-source sensor heterogeneity, seasonal dynamics, and mixed canopy conditions within 10 m pixels. We propose MiMNet-STASF, a spatiotemporal fusion framework for grid-level canopy-structure inversion from 24-month Sentinel-1/2 time series. The framework integrates a nested Mamba architecture (Inner VMamba for multi-scale spatial encoding and Outer bidirectional Mamba for long-range temporal dependency modeling), an adaptive Spatiotemporal Arbiter Gated Fusion (STASF) module (SG/TG/STAG), and a physics-informed hierarchical regression head that jointly estimates FCH and vertical structural fractions (<10 m, 10–20 m, and ≥20 m). Using UAV LiDAR-derived supervision, validated in Xiong’an New Area against 13 deep learning models spanning four architectural paradigms (RNNs, CNNs, Transformers, SSMs), MiMNet-STASF outperforms all comparatives, achieving an R2 of 0.8963 and an RMSE of 1.0903 m for FCH retrieval. Ablation results indicate that the nested Mamba and STASF components provide clearer gains on structurally imbalanced targets. From a data perspective, Sentinel-1 provides enhanced structural sensitivity, Sentinel-2 offers stable spectral and phenological context, and vegetation indices (VI) further improve vegetation contrast; their fusion enhances prediction consistency across canopy-height gradients and vertical fractional components. Moreover, MiMNet-STASF retains robust structural representations under seasonal vegetation variation. Together with cross-regional GEDI-referenced evaluation, these results support MiMNet-STASF as an effective and scalable solution for management-oriented, fine-grained urban forest canopy-structure mapping. The implementation of the proposed method is publicly available at https://github.com/qinjs123/MiMNet-STASF.

title: DCMArb: Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Hyperspectral Super-resolution

abstracts: Hyperspectral imagery (HSI) super-resolution (SR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. However, existing methods typically apply homogeneous processing to spatial-spectral features, leading to heterogeneity conflicts at the physical level. Specifically, the spatial dimension primarily exhibits locally continuous long-range dependencies, while the spectral dimension presents non-stationary and non-linear irregular coupling characteristics driven by the physical responses of ground objects. Such homogeneous feature extraction approaches lead to mutual interference between spatial structures and spectral correlations during modeling. This, in turn, results in limitations such as spatial blur and spectral drift in the reconstructed outcomes, as well as insufficient generalization and adaptability in continuous scale mapping. To alleviate the aforementioned challenges, this paper proposes an arbitrary-scale SR network named DCMArb (Decoupled-Collaborative Mamba for Arbitrary-scale Super-resolution), based on a decoupled-collaborative-reconstruction paradigm. In specific implementation, this method tightly integrates physical mechanism analysis with network module design. First, the multi-dimensional dependency extraction stage (MDES) is proposed as the decoupling unit. It separates spatial long-range dependencies and spectral non-linear correlations through differentiated modeling to avoid the mutual interference between heterogeneous features, establishing a pure feature representation foundation. Next, the heterogeneous feature integration stage (HFIS) is designed as the collaborative unit. It introduces an adaptive mechanism to dynamically balance the decoupled pure features and filtered key details, thereby constructing a high-quality, interference-resistant spatial-spectral joint prior. Finally, the scale-aware meta-learned upsampler block (SMUB) is constructed as the reconstruction unit. Utilizing a mixture-of-experts mechanism, it maps this high-quality prior to a manifold function in the continuous scale space and performs high-fidelity arbitrary-scale (including non-integer) continuous reconstruction, thereby mitigating distortion issues in cross-scale transformations. Extensive experiments on three benchmarks demonstrate that DCMArb achieves competitive or superior performance compared with state-of-the-art single-scale and arbitrary-scale methods in both quantitative metrics and visual quality. Ablation studies and complexity analyses further validate that the proposed framework achieves superior performance and generalization with reduced computational costs. The source code will be made available at https://github.com/wangswhu/DCMArb.

title: WaveUNet: An efficient deep network based on discrete wavelet transform and attention mechanism for InSAR phase unwrapping

abstracts: Phase unwrapping (PU) is a core yet challenging step in interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) measurements. Traditional PU methods rely on the assumption of phase continuity, which often fails in areas with steep topography, dense fringes, or severe decorrelation noise. While deep learning has emerged to address this limitation, existing networks suffer from two key drawbacks: (1) limited generalization due to training data that inadequately captures the complexity of real-world deformation, and (2) high computational costs caused by the use of deep architectures with extensive parameters and high-dimensional convolutions to pursue accuracy. These two factors lead to the insufficient generalization capability and considerable consumption of computing resources for these networks. To address these issues, this study presents a lightweight deep phase unwrapping network based on the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and attention mechanism, called WaveUNet. To train this network, we first simulate InSAR phase data to generate a sample dataset encompassing complex topographic and deformation features; subsequently, WaveUNet is trained by integrating the DWT and attention mechanism, achieving phase unwrapping with high precision and less computational resources; finally, we conduct tests on WaveUNet using the simulated dataset, the InSAR-DLPU dataset, and real InSAR data. The experimental results demonstrate that the GPU usage of WaveUNet is 32.96%, 24.43%, and 38.63% of that for VURNet, ResUNet, and PUNet, respectively. Meanwhile, its total number of floating-point operations (FLOPs) is merely 21.80%, 23.81%, and 9.23% of that for the three models, respectively. This illustrates that WaveUNet achieves comparable accuracy and efficiency to state-of-the-art PU models while utilizing limited computational resources. The related experimental code will be made available at https://github.com/xiangHQ/WaveUNet.git.

title: TALineNet: A benchmark and network for temporally-aware continuous line segment detection in event streams

Experimental results demonstrate that TALineNet achieves 57.7% msAP on the Ev-LineSeq dataset, outperforming the state-of-the-art by 12.9 percentage points. abstracts: Event cameras offer unique advantages for line segment detection in high-speed and high-dynamic-range scenarios, yet existing methods face two critical limitations. They primarily operate on isolated event frames, overlooking temporal continuity and unstable imaging within continuous streams. Furthermore, the lack of absolute intensity renders these methods highly susceptible to noise, hindering reliable spatial feature extraction. To bridge this gap, we first establish two novel benchmarks, Ev-WireframeSeq (synthetic) and Ev-LineSeq (real-world), providing the first sequential event-based line segment detection datasets with dense line annotations to facilitate temporal context learning. Supported by these benchmarks, we propose TALineNet, a temporally-aware network that delivers temporally consistent and spatially robust line segment detection from continuous event streams. The network leverages a recurrent backbone to capture long-range temporal dependencies and employs a background-line disentanglement (BLD) module to suppress noise and emphasize true edge structures. Moreover, a Bézier-based representation is adopted in the detection head to better accommodate the non-uniform spatial distributions in event data. To quantitatively assess detection stability over time, we introduce a set of sequence-level evaluation metrics, including the Geometric Stability Score (GSS) and Temporal Fidelity Index (TFI). Experimental results demonstrate that TALineNet achieves 57.7% msAP on the Ev-LineSeq dataset, outperforming the state-of-the-art by 12.9 percentage points. The source code and datasets are available at https://github.com/Qiuben/TALineNet.

title: Segmentation-guided and attention-enhanced GAN for SAR image restoration under multi-type interference

The source code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/XIAOYU-XU2805/SC2-GAN.

abstracts: Spaceborne synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems are often affected by co-frequency interference, which significantly degrades imaging quality and subsequent image interpretation performance. Existing suppression methods typically focus on a single interference type or salient interference, which limits their effectiveness when confronted with multi-type real-measured interference. To address these challenges, this paper reformulates the multi-type interference suppression problem as a pre-imaging clean SAR echo restoration task, and proposes a novel SC2-GAN framework for SAR imaging. Built upon a generative adversarial network, SC2-GAN integrates three synergistic components: segmentation-guided mechanism (SGM), convolutional block attention module (CBAM), and conditionally parameterized convolution module (CondConv). The SGM extracts the spatial location and type information of interference in shallow feature space, enabling differentiated attention to multiple interference types. CBAM captures discriminative features in both channel and spatial through dual attention mechanisms, enhancing the network’s ability to perceive interference features in deeper layers. CondConv adaptively generates convolutional kernels according to input features, enabling the network to respond differently to diverse interference intensities and patterns in the parameter space. The synergy of these components forms the foundation of SC2-GAN’s adaptability to multi-type and multi-intensity interference. In addition, SC2-GAN achieves accurate interference suppression and segmentation in an end-to-end manner using a shared network architecture. Experiments conducted on seven simulated datasets and ten real-measured Sentinel-1 datasets demonstrate that the proposed SC2-GAN can suppress multiple types of interference and improved SAR imaging quality. The source code and datasets are publicly available at: https://github.com/XIAOYU-XU2805/SC2-GAN.

title: PELNet: A general physics-embedded learning framework for polarimetric target decomposition

links.context: multi-band PolSAR datasets across diverse terrain types demonstrate that PELNet achieves superior accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional methods, providing a new perspective for PolSAR image interpretation and physical parameter inversion. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/shurongz/PhyDecomp.

abstracts: Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) provides full polarimetric measurements, from which physically meaningful scattering parameters can be derived through target decomposition. Traditional model-driven methods often suffer from rigid power allocation, sensitivity to noise, and limited capability in representing complex scattering scenes. In contrast, deep learning-based approaches can learn intricate scattering patterns directly from data with greater flexibility. Nevertheless, these purely data-driven methods usually model scattering mechanisms as black boxes, resulting in limited physical interpretability and reduced generalization to complex or unseen scenarios. Building on these observations, we investigate the integration of physical priors into deep neural networks and propose PELNet, a physics-embedded end-to-end framework for polarimetric target decomposition. The core innovation of PELNet lies in structurally embedding a differentiable scattering model within the network decoder, establishing a strict correspondence between the latent space and interpretable physical parameters. Specifically, a multi-scale SE-attention encoder is used to extract context-aware polarimetric features, while a lightweight Mixture-of-Experts module enables adaptive modeling of different volume scattering components. Furthermore, a differentiable scattering reconstruction layer embeds the physical scattering model directly into the network decoder, establishing an interpretable mapping between latent representations and physical parameters. A physically guided loss function is further introduced to enhance reconstruction fidelity and spatial consistency. Experiments on multi-band PolSAR datasets across diverse terrain types demonstrate that PELNet achieves superior accuracy and interpretability compared to traditional methods, providing a new perspective for PolSAR image interpretation and physical parameter inversion. The source code and pretrained models are publicly available at https://github.com/shurongz/PhyDecomp.

title: PatchFusion: Resilient LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation in autonomous driving

links.context: rruptions. Extensive experiments on well-known datasets in autonomous driving (SemanticKITTI and nuScenes) demonstrate that PatchFusion can effectively improve the performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion for 3D semantic segmentation on both clean and corrupted datasets. The relevant code will be available at https://github.com/sssssyf/PatchFusion.

abstracts: LiDAR-camera fusion for point cloud semantic segmentation is essential for accurate and reliable 3D perception of autonomous driving systems. Contemporary LiDAR-camera fusion approaches predominantly integrate the pixel-level camera features located by projected points to augment the corresponding 3D points, which can be abstractly defined as point-pixel fusion strategy. Although such point-pixel fusion mode has been proved to be effective and widely used in practice, the strategy has two non-ignorable defects: (1) dependent on precise point-pixel projection correspondence, (2) limited by just using extremely little image information. Besides, the LiDAR-only inference in offline fusion fails to utilize the synchronously obtained images to achieve a dynamic fusion for 3D perception, while LiDAR-camera fusion inference in online fusion still encounters challenges of field of view (FoV) discrepancy between sensors. Moreover, the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods for 3D semantic segmentation, a crucial factor for the practical reliability of perception systems, has received limited attention. Thus, focusing on addressing above challenges, we develop the point-patch fusion mode, and construct PatchFusion framework as a systematic and promising solution to enhance performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion perception in realistic and complex driving scenes. Specifically, in PatchFusion, we propose to leverage cross-attention mechanism to implement high-quality point-patch fusion by automatically searching what information should be highlighted or suppressed from the local patch of image, thereby alleviating the adverse effects of projection errors, maximizing the utilization of the high-density image information, and being more robust to the potential image corruptions. Besides, we integrate the strengths of offline and online fusion modes and propose a bidirectional cross-modality knowledge distillation strategy, aiming to further enhance the performance and robustness for predictions within and outside camera FoV. Finally, to bridge the research gap regarding the corruption robustness of LiDAR-camera fusion methods, we design a specialized dataset corruption suite for public multimodal datasets to simulate complex evaluation conditions by synthesizing projection noises and image corruptions. Extensive experiments on well-known datasets in autonomous driving (SemanticKITTI and nuScenes) demonstrate that PatchFusion can effectively improve the performance and resilience of LiDAR-camera fusion for 3D semantic segmentation on both clean and corrupted datasets. The relevant code will be available at https://github.com/sssssyf/PatchFusion.

title: Continuous-time causal distribution learning with identifiability for brain dynamic effective connectivity inference

abstracts: Dynamic effective connectivity (dEC) analysis provides an approach for revealing the causal mechanism of information transmission in human brain. However, existing discrete-time dEC learning models suffer a mismatch between sampling and causal frequencies as well as low efficiency in data utilization. Based on a continuous-time dynamic causality distribution learning framework, we propose a dEC distribution learning model, which uses free energy principle to ensure more proper parameter learning than maximum likelihood estimation. Theoretically, the identifiability of the proposed model is proved, which guarantees the uniqueness of the learned dEC given the same data distribution. Results from the synthetic dataset show that the ability in both causality learning and time series reconstruction of the proposed model outperforms the comparison methods. The dEC results learned from the task functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) data reveal the changing information transmission patterns in brain when dealing with picture-sentence matching tasks. Additionally, during the transition from resting state to task state, information flow in the brain's dEC network becomes increasingly organized around the left supramarginal gyrus, a hub known for the language processing and information integration in parietal lobe. When applied to resting-state fMRI data on Alzheimer's disease, the learned dEC patterns reveal distinct alterations in brain networks associated with Alzheimer's disease. The results suggest that Alzheimer's disease is associated with abnormalities not only in memory and emotion-related networks, but also in networks underlying executive control and visual integration. The source code of the proposed model are available at https://github.com/Yiding00/IDECD-CT.

title: Unsupervised denoising of diffusion-weighted images with bias and variance corrected noise modeling

links.context: ethods on simulated and in vivo dMRI data demonstrate that the proposed approach yields higher image quality and more reliable diffusion metrics. These results highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for Rician noise-induced bias and heteroscedasticity in magnitude-domain dMRI denoising. Code is available at https://github.com/XieJine/Rician-Moment-DIP.

abstracts: Diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (dMRI) plays a vital role in both clinical diagnostics and neuroscience research. However, its inherently low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), especially under high diffusion weighting, substantially degrades image quality and impairs downstream analysis. Recent self-supervised and unsupervised denoising approaches have shown promising potential without requiring clean reference images. However, most of these methods neglect the non-Gaussian statistical characteristics of noise in magnitude dMRI data, leading to biased estimation and suboptimal optimization under heteroscedastic noise. To address this limitation, we propose two Rician noise-aware loss functions that explicitly account for these characteristics. One loss function is derived from the first-order moment of the Rician distribution for signal bias correction, while the other leverages the second-order moment to perform bias correction through squared-signal statistics. Each loss further incorporates adaptive weighting based on the signal-dependent Rician noise variance to address heteroscedasticity. The proposed objectives are instantiated within an image-specific, unsupervised Deep Image Prior (DIP) framework without modifying the network architecture. Comparisons with state-of-the-art denoising methods on simulated and in vivo dMRI data demonstrate that the proposed approach yields higher image quality and more reliable diffusion metrics. These results highlight the importance of explicitly accounting for Rician noise-induced bias and heteroscedasticity in magnitude-domain dMRI denoising. Code is available at https://github.com/XieJine/Rician-Moment-DIP.

abstracts: Large Atomistic Models (LAMs) have undergone remarkable progress recently, emerging as universal or fundamental representations of the potential energy surface defined by the first-principles calculations of atomistic systems. However, our understanding of the extent to which these models achieve true universality, as well as their comparative performance across different models, remains limited. This gap is largely due to the lack of comprehensive benchmarks capable of evaluating the effectiveness of LAMs as approximations to the universal potential energy surface. In this study, we introduce LAMBench, a benchmarking system designed to evaluate LAMs in terms of their generalizability, adaptability, and applicability. These attributes are crucial for deploying LAMs as ready-to-use tools across a diverse array of scientific discovery contexts. We benchmark ten state-of-the-art LAMs released prior to August 1, 2025, using LAMBench. Our findings reveal a significant gap between the current LAMs and the ideal universal potential energy surface. They also highlight the need for incorporating cross-domain training data, supporting multi-fidelity modeling, and ensuring the models’ conservativeness and differentiability. As a dynamic and extensible platform, LAMBench is intended to continuously evolve, thereby facilitating the development of robust and generalizable LAMs capable of significantly advancing scientific research. The LAMBench code is open-sourced at https://github.com/deepmodeling/lambench , and an interactive leaderboard is available at https://www.aissquare.com/openlam?tab=Benchmark .

abstracts: As industrial equipment is increasingly applied in manufacturing, it is necessary to adopt advanced maintenance techniques to ensure stable equipment operation. Maintenance decision support is essential for industrial equipment, but information fragmentation and complex reasoning hinder its progress. To address these challenges, we propose MAKG (Multi-Agent and synergistic Knowledge Graph), a framework that synergizes Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a multi-agent system for intelligent industrial equipment maintenance. The MAKG framework uses these Large Language Models (LLM) agents to work together, drawing information from a diverse knowledge base to produce coordinated responses to equipment faults. Our method focuses on fine-tuning the embedding models with domain-specific data. This approach avoids the high computational cost of re-training the entire LLM and improves performance in the specific industrial context. In the experimental study, the MAKG framework was validated using real-world industrial operation and maintenance data, achieving a reasoning accuracy of 90.1% and demonstrating its potential for intelligent maintenance of industrial equipment. Code is available at https://github.com/LAM2360/MAKG_demo/tree/master.

abstracts: Efficient recycling and reuse of end-of-life products through robot-assisted disassembly has attracted widespread attention in sustainable manufacturing industry. In the robot-assisted disassembly system, the high-precision identification of products and their components is the premise of autonomous disassembly. A series of product identification methods based on deep learning in literature can well identify specific categories of components such as screws. However, different service conditions make products in industrial scenarios highly uncertain in terms of component status, shape and position changes, which make it impossible to predefine categories for products and components, and to obtain high-quality training data sets for new categories in advance. These obstacles make the application of the identification methods to industrial scenarios still challenging. In this paper, a two-stage product identification method based on neural–symbolic reasoning is proposed. In the first stage, deep learning-based methods are used to detect component primitives with limited categories, rather than directly detecting components whose categories cannot be predefined. In the second stage, the logic rules embedded in the word vector space are used to program the detected primitives to infer the semantics of the component to be detected. In addition, a primitive sampling method is proposed to generate new rules by sampling existing rules in the word vector space to improve the generalization of the proposed identification method. The results show a significant increase from 20.01% to 80.89% in successful component identification for the PC product family, along with considerable improvement for others. Code and data are available at http://github.com/nowheresin/neural-symbolic-reasoning-product-identification/.

abstracts: In the autonomy problem of large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing orders, three steps are usually involved: allocating orders among enterprises, assigning parts to 3D printers, and arranging parts on the printer’s build platform. Among these steps, the layout of parts on a 3D printer serves as the underlying layer of the autonomy loop, providing the basis for obtaining feedback during part-equipment matching and enabling real-time adjustments. It also affects the allocation of orders among enterprises. Currently, artificial intelligence (AI) agents specifically designed for part layout remain underdeveloped, and practical engineering applications still rely heavily on manual operations. Against this backdrop, this paper proposes a novel reinforcement-learning-enhanced autonomous layout method for 3D printing parts using a small-parameter vision-language model (SPVLM), aiming to provide an effective AI agent solution for the autonomous parts layout stage. We propose an autonomy architecture for large-scale, mass-customized 3D printing. For the part layout problem in 3D printing, we propose a visual-text evidence enhancement method and construct a dataset of 10,000 scene samples. We further propose an improved generative reinforcement policy optimization (GRPO) technique to enhance the layout decision-making capability of SPVLMs. Finally, based on the SPVLM, we build an AI agent using a reasoning and acting (ReAct) architecture. The AI agent continually acquires part-layout experience through a memory-augmentation strategy and supports lightweight deployment. A representative subset of the dataset is made publicly available at: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RTYGFb2dvBAsXXD5v7OTXq07QpIXMcTA?usp=drive_link

abstracts: This research is motivated by the need to predict cavity length in ventilated cavitation experiments. Given the freestream velocity and ventilation rate, the underlying physical mechanism gives rise to informative bounds and distinct shedding regimes, which in turn induce nonstationarity in the system. In this paper, we propose a novel nonstationary bounded Gaussian process regression model that simultaneously incorporates nonstationarity and bound constraints. We adopt the Gaussian process projection framework to enforce the bound constraints and propose a mixture of bounded Gaussian processes to capture nonstationarity, where each component models a locally stationary behavior consistent with the constraints. The model parameters and mixture components are estimated through a two-stage procedure. Importantly, the proposed model reveals latent physical mechanisms by identifying distinct components, thereby offering deeper scientific insights into the input-output relationship. Numerical results across test functions and the ventilated cavitation experiments validate the superiority of the proposed method. Specifically, the proposed method effectively captures the evolution of ventilated cavity structures, thereby significantly enhancing the adaptability and operational reliability of high-speed underwater vehicles under complex environmental conditions. Codes are available on https://github.com/tbai114/Nonstationary-bounded-Gaussian-process.
